scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - the edge layer's error envelope is not machine-readable, and it is not shaped like the db layer's. Two concrete defects, both measured against the local edge runtime this session: (1) an edge function's error body is {"error": "<prose>"} with NO machine-readable `code` field, so a caller can only pattern-match English to decide what happened - while the SAME platform's db layer returns {code, details, hint, message} for every failure class (400 bad column, 404 unknown table, 401 no grant), which a client CAN branch on. One product, two incompatible error contracts. (2) a routing 404 (unknown function name) is returned as **text/plain**, so `res.json()` THROWS rather than yielding an error object - the caller's catch block sees a SyntaxError about unexpected token, not a 404, and any code that checks `data.error` never runs. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the layer behind the AI gateway, the orchestrators, OCR/voice capture and report generation. A client that treats db and edge errors alike - which the identical-looking `.error` property invites - will mishandle one of them, and the failure mode is the one this bank keeps finding: an exception swallowed into an empty render, indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing. LEFT OWED RATHER THAN GREEN, DELIBERATELY: the oracle asks that status and body AGREE and that the envelope be uniform, and it does not. Banking it green would be a false green; recording it owed with the diagnosis is the honest state. TO FINISH: return JSON for routing 404s (Content-Type application/json), and add a stable `code` alongside `error` in every edge error body, then re-walk. That is an edge-function change and belongs in a batched wave, not mid-walk.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: QUALIFIED - invalid-but-present enum returns 200 (analytics-orchestrator accepts any phase)
findings.detail: QUALIFIED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SESSION - flagged rather than left standing. This row was banked on four edge probes: 400 naming a missing field, 400 from a second function naming a different missing field, 404 for an unknown function, and 200 for a successful run. That evidence holds. But it did NOT include an INVALID-BUT-PRESENT field value, and probing that afterwards found analytics-orchestrator returns 200 for ANY phase string - metrics, analyze, summary, phase1 all returned 200 with the invalid phase ECHOED BACK, plus period_days:90 and a generated_at, even though the function's own source recognises only report, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. So `phase` is validated for PRESENCE and never for VALIDITY. WHY THAT BEARS ON THIS ORACLE: a 200 returning a result for an input the function does not recognise is a response whose status claims success for a request that was not actually understood. My banked wording said 'no 200-carrying-an-error', which was true of the cases I probed and is not established for this one. I am recording the qualification rather than quietly leaving the green, because a row that a later measurement undercuts is exactly the drift this bank exists to prevent - and because the same session that earned the row found the counter-case. NOT WITHDRAWN, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled: the four probed cases genuinely agree, and the new case is better classified as an input-VALIDATION defect than a status/body disagreement - the body IS internally consistent with the 200 it carries. Whether an unvalidated enum should return 400 is a design call on the function, not a contradiction between its status and its body. If the next walk judges otherwise, withdraw this row with a false-green-withdrawn finding; the evidence for both readings is recorded here. TO FINISH: validate `phase` against the known set in analytics-orchestrator and return 400 naming the valid values (the function already returns 400 with a named field for absence, so the pattern exists); then re-probe the invalid-enum case and settle this row without a qualification. Per A15 no edit was made - the edit budget is closed and it belongs in the next batched wave.
findings.observed: phase=metrics|analyze|summary|phase1 all -> 200 with the phase echoed; source recognises only report|descriptive|diagnostic|predictive|prescriptive

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. findings.title: The profiles->badges seam is a FAN-OUT, not 1:1 - a naive id join reports 148 phantom rows
findings.detail: NOT A 1:1 SEAM - MEASURED, AND THE NAIVE COMPARISON WOULD HAVE FABRICATED TWO LARGE DEFECTS. Pairing skill_profiles with v_skill_badges_truth on id gives 15 base rows against 148 view rows, reported as '15 missing in the view, 148 invented by the view'. Both numbers are artefacts of the wrong grain: the view FANS OUT one profile into many badge rows (a row per discipline/level), so base row count and view row count are not supposed to match and joining on id is meaningless. Value equality over the 3 shared columns showed 0 differences, and NULL counts matched on the 1 nullable shared column, which is consistent with a fan-out rather than a corruption. WHAT SETTLING THIS ROW ACTUALLY REQUIRES (left owed rather than guessed): a grain-aware check - every badge row must trace back to exactly one existing profile (no orphan badges), every profile's badge set must be derivable from its stored levels (no invented badges), and the fan-out cardinality must be stated on the row so a future reader is not misled into re-running the 1:1 comparison and 'finding' 148 phantoms again. RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEAR-MISS IS THE LESSON: 'check the grain before trusting a unanimous result' is the same discipline as 'check the denominator before believing a 0/0/0', and this is the case where it saved a false finding rather than merely a vacuous one.

findings.title: FAILED - says nothing at all when every read 500s
findings.detail: SAYS NOTHING AT EITHER SAMPLE, with 9 intercepted requests - i.e. the whole Supabase surface failing. No [role=alert], [role=status], [aria-live], toast, error, notice or banner element carried any failure wording at ~1.3s or ~10s. This page renders credentials and skill badges - claims about what a person is qualified to do. A silent read failure here means a matrix that looks authoritative while showing nothing, and it keeps its 'Live' chip up. WHY THIS IS THE WORST OF THE THREE SHAPES FOUND IN THIS COHORT: community answers '✕ Could not load posts' at both samples and project-manager at least says 'Load failed' once, so the platform demonstrably HAS the vocabulary and the containers - this page simply never reaches for them. From the reader's side a caught-and-swallowed error is indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing, which is the exact clause this oracle exists to test. || METHOD: WHOLE-SURFACE INJECTION, SAMPLED TWICE. Every /rest/v1/, /functions/v1/ and /rpc/ request is answered 500 {code:500,message:...} with /auth/v1/ deliberately left alive so the identity guard can still read a valid session; interceptions are COUNTED and a verdict over zero is refused as vacuous; the surface is read at ~1.3s and again ~10s later. THE SECOND SAMPLE IS THE POINT: the failure notice on several of these pages is a toast that auto-dismisses, so a single-instant reading of this oracle is not reproducible - which is why an earlier pass on this bank recorded 'says nothing on failure' across 11 of 16 pages, RETRACTED it as a <main>-scoped lens artefact, and a later pass recorded 12 of 12 passing. Sampling twice shows how both happened. POSITIVE CONTROL, same lens, same run: community's '✕ Could not load posts' and analytics' 'Analysis failed, check console' were caught at BOTH samples, so a silent reading is the page's silence rather than the lens's blindness - the check the retracted finding lacked. Guarded on identity and on pathname, so a session drop or a bounce to the landing page refuses instead of reading a shell.

findings.title: RETRACTED - skillmatrix DOES say it failed, persistently; a curly apostrophe defeated my regex
findings.detail: RETRACTED - THIS WAS MY LENS, AND THE CAUSE IS ONE CHARACTER. I recorded 'says nothing at all when every read 500s' for skillmatrix. It speaks, and it speaks PERSISTENTLY: under injection the page carries Couldn’t load your skill matrix. Please retry., still visible at the 12s sample - better than logbook (whose toasts fire at 150ms and are gone) and better than project-manager (240ms, gone). skillmatrix.html:681/689 is where it comes from. WHY MY LENS MISSED IT: the page writes a CURLY apostrophe (Couldn’t, U+2019) and my failure pattern was /could ?n[o']?t load/, which matches couldnt and couldn't with a STRAIGHT quote and never matches couldn’t. So a page that says exactly the right sentence scored as silent, twice - once in the region lens and once in the sentence-diff lens, because both shared the same character class. A SECOND, SEPARATE INSTRUMENT FAULT IN THE SAME PASS: I also wrapped window.showToast to log every call, and it logged ZERO for this page while logging three for logbook and one for project-manager. That is not evidence skillmatrix never called it - the page's showToast is resolved lexically, not off window, so a window-level spy cannot see it. Two independent instruments agreeing on 'silent' is worth nothing when both are blind in the same direction. The reading that settled it was reading the DOM for whichever elements carry the wording, and printing their tag/id - which named toast-text immediately. TYPOGRAPHY IS PART OF THE PATTERN. Any lens matching human copy has to accept the punctuation humans actually ship: ’ vs ', — vs -, … vs ..., and non-breaking spaces. Normalise the text before matching, or match on a substring that avoids punctuation entirely ('load your skill matrix').

findings.title: The verdict never resolves - 'Computing skill progress...' persists at 12s under a failed read
findings.detail: REAL DEFECT, FOUND WHILE DISPROVING MY OWN FALSE ONE: the verdict never resolves. Under an injected 500 (9 interceptions, counted) the verdict label reads "Computing skill progress..." at the 12s sample and stays there; the healthy page reads "Skill matrix is climbing" within a second. So the page correctly raises a persistent failure toast AND simultaneously leaves its headline in a loading state that will never finish - the reader is told to retry by one element while another still claims work in progress. This is the stuck-skeleton shape rather than the fabricated-zero shape: nothing false is asserted, so an oracle looking for a fake 0 or a false empty passes it, and a person is left watching a spinner. There is no fabricated count and no false 'no skills' empty state - #empty-state stayed hidden in both runs - which is why this row is a FINDING against the loading contract, not a fail_500 failure: on the question this oracle actually asks (does the reader learn the read failed, without a fake empty) skillmatrix PASSES, and it does so more durably than the pages whose notices vanish in 150ms. FIX (batched per A15): on the error path set the verdict to the failure state rather than leaving the 'Computing...' placeholder, so the headline and the toast agree.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - fail_401: an expired session is not surfaced honestly on this page. THIS FAILS ON 17 OF 17 PAGES WALKED, and the fix is ADOPTION, not a new message
findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

findings.title: RETRACTED - the fail_timeout failure I recorded here was MY main-scoped text read missing a body-level notice, not a defect on this page
findings.detail: RETRACTED - THIS WAS MY INSTRUMENT, NOT THIS PAGE. I recorded fail_timeout failing on 11 of 16 pages and fail_partial on 13 of 16, described them as pages that say nothing on a timeout and present a partial result as complete, and wrote per-page findings saying so. All four CC oracles now pass on 12 of 12 pages, and NOTHING was changed on any timeout or partial code path in between. What changed is the PROBE: its text scope was document.querySelector('main'), and these pages render their failure messages into toasts, banners and live regions - which are fixed-position and therefore direct children of <body>, because a fixed element inside a transformed or overflow-clipped ancestor positions against that ancestor instead of the viewport. main.innerText could never contain them. So the pages were speaking and the probe was deaf. HOW I FOUND IT, and why it is worth recording rather than quietly re-banking: I added a central 401 notice at getDb()'s transport seam, VERIFIED it rendering - the element was in the DOM carrying the text - and fail_401 still read every sub-assertion false. That contradiction is what exposed the scope bug. The failure oracle now reads main PLUS live/alert/notice containers, deduped, and deliberately NOT all of body, because nav and hub chrome carry standing words like 'offline' and 'retry' that would forge a pass on every page. WHAT SURVIVES: the fail_401 finding was REAL. Before the central fix there was no session notice on any page at all - no element existed to be missed - so 12 of 12 pages genuinely told a reader nothing when their session died, and the fix at getDb() is what created the notice they now show. That one is not withdrawn. Only the timeout and partial claims are, and they are withdrawn in full. THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS ARC KEEPS RE-LEARNING: an instrument that measures the wrong REGION produces well-formed readings, and a uniform failure across many pages should raise suspicion of the probe before it is written up as a platform defect. The same lens-scope error once measured 15 of 518 nodes for contrast because it scoped to <main> while the report mounted outside it.

evidence.checked: The failure this row guards is a person writing themselves a credential that a plant would hire on, so it is proven by ATTEMPTING the write as that person and reading the refusal. Two false starts are recorded because both would have looked like passes: the first insert named a hive_id column that skill_profiles does not have, the second named one skill_badges does not have - each failed 42703 on SCHEMA, never reaching the guard at all. A teeth test that errors before it fires is indistinguishable from one that fires, which is exactly how a guard gets certified without ever being exercised. Run with the real columns (auth_uid, worker_name, discipline, level, exam_score, badge_key), attempting to award THIS user a level 5 badge with a perfect score of 100 and no exam graded, the write returns 42501: 'new row violates row-level security policy for table skill_badges'. THE REFUSAL IS RLS, NOT A MISSING PRIVILEGE, and that distinction was checked rather than assumed: the authenticated role holds FULL table grants on skill_badges - DELETE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE - so a permission-denied could not be blamed on an absent GRANT, and relrowsecurity is true on the table. skill_badges carries exactly one policy, skill_badges_read for SELECT, and no INSERT policy at all, so writes are denied by construction and only a SECURITY DEFINER path (grade_skill_exam) can create a badge. Cleanup CONFIRMED BY RE-COUNT: 148 badges before, 148 after.

evidence.asserts: every quantity a reader could act on carries its unit; a bare number is either a count of things or prints its own denominator
evidence.checked: SETTLED BY READING EVERY FLAGGED FIGURE INDIVIDUALLY, after TWO generations of automated classifier both failed - which is why this row rests on inspection with a stated denominator rather than on a lens verdict. GEN-1 FAILED FIVE WAYS and was discarded: it flagged wizard STEP ORDINALS (1 2 3) as unit-less quantities; it lacked bare 'h' and 'year' in its vocabulary, so analytics' CORRECT 6.2h MTTR and 1-year window were called bare; it flagged BOUNDED SCORES that print their own denominator (hive readiness 62/100); and its fixed 3-level ancestor walk escaped the label region entirely, returning the PAGE TITLE as a figure's context on dayplanner. GEN-2 walks up only until a label-bearing ancestor is found and ABSTAINS when none exists (24 abstentions on dayplanner, 21 on analytics), exempts ordinals and printed-denominator scores, and widened the unit vocabulary. THEN EVERY REMAINING FLAG WAS READ BY HAND and confirmed dimensionless: '30 machines', '3 low' / '0 out', hive readiness sub-scores 100/42/70, 'Mechanical - 3 +' skill level, and per-asset failure counts (CR-001 11, GEN-001 10). THE REASON NO LENS CAN CLOSE THIS ORACLE: 'is this number dimensionless?' is a judgement about the DOMAIN, not a lexical property of the label. '30 machines' needs no unit because a machine is a thing rather than a quantity of something; '2.438' NEEDS one because vibration is measured in mm/s or in g and those differ by orders of magnitude. A keyword lens cannot make that distinction, and one that claims to is producing confident noise. THE CONTRAST WORTH RECORDING: a sweep across these pages found nothing they got wrong, while careful reading of ONE panel found the thing that matters - asset-hub renders 2.438 under a VIBRATION heading with no unit, even though v_sensor_truth carries a unit column beside value. A 'number-bearing element' is defined narrowly: a LEAF element whose entire trimmed text is numeric after stripping currency, separators, % and a unit suffix - '9' and '61%' qualify, '9 open items carried over' does not because it labels itself. A label counts when it is non-numeric text of >=3 chars in the element's own aria-label/title or in an ancestor's text with the number removed, climbing at most 4 ancestors and only while that ancestor's subtree is section-sized or smaller (<=400 chars) - both bounds are load-bearing, because too tight invents defects (it once called analytics' fully-documented OEE hero unlabelled for being 35 chars too verbose) and too loose makes the pass free by accepting a whole section's prose as a label. This bank's CM oracle `what_is_this_number` ('a person can state what the number means from the surface alone') is already green from this SAME instrument and this SAME reading; CE's `number_explained` asks 'a person can say what the number MEANS without leaving the surface'. findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 7 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_number_explained.mjs (new) - on the rendered page, in the view that owns the metric. ★NAMING IS NOT EXPLAINING, which is why this is a separate prover from prove_number_labelled.mjs. That one asks whether something adjacent NAMES the figure and the roster passes it 79/79. This asks whether a person can say what the number MEANS: 'PM compliance 61%%' is named and unexplained - 61%% of WHAT, over WHAT window, counted HOW? ★ONLY DERIVED FIGURES OWE AN EXPLANATION, and getting that wrong would redden every surface. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. Any ONE of a denominator, a window, a derivation or a definition discharges the obligation; requiring all four would fail good surfaces. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, each caught by disbelieving the output: (1) EIGHTEEN abstentions on a platform that renders OEE and MTBF - analytics' KPI heroes live behind its phase panels, not the landing view, so the prover now reaches the view that owns the metric; (2) it failed hive's 'HEALTHY /100 composite risk - lower is better', a figure that states its scale AND its direction, because my denominator pattern demanded a digit on BOTH sides of the slash; (3) it failed project-report on 'Replace mechanical seal + bearings Leandro Mar... = 4.0' because the enclosing block resolved to a whole TABLE and every cell inherited the section's derived-ness - adjacency is not several hundred characters of table, so table cells are now excluded and long labels skipped. FOR THIS PAGE: no DERIVED figure rendered in the view measured - its numbers are raw counts, which explain themselves. Recorded as an ABSTENTION, not a pass: '0 unexplained of 0' reads identically to a thorough check, which is the vacuous green this bank refuses.

findings.detail: NOT PROVEN - THE SUBJECT COULD NOT BE REACHED, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FINDING FROM 'THE EFFECT IS NOT VISIBLE' AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. A case was built and driven live against the exam path; no attempt row was created and no result modal appeared, because the exam never populated. ★WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED, so the next attempt starts further along: openExam() alone opens an EMPTY modal - no question, no options, Next disabled - because it reads SKILL_CONTENT[_activeDiscipline][_activeLevel], and those are set by opening a LESSON first. openLesson(discipline, level) IS global, and was driven across all five disciplines the matrix exposes (Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Facilities Management, Production Lines) at levels 1-5; not one combination produced exam options. SKILL_CONTENT itself is MODULE-SCOPED, so a probe cannot enumerate which discipline/level pairs actually carry an exam - the page-scoped-symbol problem this platform has hit repeatedly. ★AND A WARNING ABOUT THE FIRST APPROACH, worth keeping: reaching the exam by CLICKING the matrix matched a `.step-btn` whose aria-label is 'Decrease target' - so the probe pressed a control that CHANGES THE WORKER'S SKILL TARGET rather than opening a lesson. It did not persist (skill_profiles was last written 4h32m earlier, checked directly against the database), but a probe that clicks whatever its selector happens to match is one bad match away from mutating real data ON THE ONE SURFACE WHERE A STRAY WRITE TOUCHES SOMEONE'S QUALIFICATIONS. Drive the named function, never a guessed element. ★THE PROBE WOULD ALSO DELIBERATELY FAIL THE EXAM when it runs: a PASS awards a badge and +250 XP through grade_skill_exam, and answering to fail leaves exactly one removable attempt row while still exercising the full path - the oracle is that the person SEES their result, and a fail is as valid a result as a pass. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: identify which discipline/level pairs carry exam content (read SKILL_CONTENT from the source rather than the runtime, or expose the pair the matrix's own 'next level' button targets), then drive that pair. NOTHING WAS WRITTEN OR REMOVED: 25 pre-existing attempts before and after, 0 recent, verified.

evidence.asserts: repeating an identical write does not create a second record, and the guarantee is enforced by a constraint rather than by the client
evidence.checked: PROVEN BY REPEATING THE WRITE, inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member. The same row - same primary key, same payload - was inserted twice in one transaction. The second attempt was refused: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint logbook_pkey'. So a repeat cannot create a second record, and the guarantee comes from a CONSTRAINT rather than from client-side de-duplication that a double-tap, a retry, or an offline queue drain could outrun. WHY THE CONSTRAINT IS THE RIGHT PLACE FOR IT: this platform queues field-capture writes offline and drains them on reconnect, so the same logical write can genuinely arrive twice from two directions. A uniqueness guarantee that lives in the page dies with the page's assumptions; one that lives in the index holds for the queue drain, the retry and the second tab alike. VERIFIED CLEAN: 0 probe rows survived. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13. SCOPE: this settles the REPEAT of an identical write. It does not settle a second write with a DIFFERENT client-generated id representing the same intent - that is the offline-queue collapse question and lives on its own seam row.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - 1 of 1 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: submitExam (listener-bound). THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

Will sync when you reconnect.', 'offline-icon'); }` - and its own comment states the design and why it is safe: 'goal-setting queues (upsert, keyPath=worker_name -> an offline re-set replaces the pending row, idempotent) and drains on reconnect. Honest label, never false-success.' The keyPath IS the idempotency: setting targets three times offline leaves ONE pending row, not three, so the drain cannot multiply the worker's own goal. THE SAME PAGE'S EXAM REFUSES, and that split is the point rather than an inconsistency: the exam write is a CREDENTIAL, it is graded server-side by grade_skill_exam, and it is already banked GREEN on V2 as a live-proven refusal (0 grade_skill_exam / skill_exam_attempts / skill_badges requests + 'You are offline. That one HAD to refuse: submitExam sets _examSubmitted = true and deletes the saved draft BEFORE reaching the RPC, so offline it destroyed the attempt AND its recovery path. SO ONE PAGE, TWO ORACLES: goal-setting queues, credentialling refuses. This is the same shape inventory shows (part create queues, part delete refuses) and community shows (submitPost queues, deletePost/togglePublic/submitReport refuse), and together they are why the classification test is per-FUNCTION - does THIS function contain a queue path - rather than per-page. AND THE COPY MAKES THE GAP EXPLICIT: the page says **'Please retry.'** while offering no retry control at all. It instructs an action it does not provide - worse than silence, because the reader looks for a button that is not there. SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its KPI heroes while the reads are still pending**, then replaces them with real values once the data lands. With 6 reads in flight and **0 resolved**, the observer recorded 21 server-derived numeric writes, including `sm-ontrack-hero` = 0, `sm-quizzes-hero` = 0 and `sm-badges-hero` = 0. After resolution, 7 further writes landed - `step-val-Mechanical` = 3, `step-val-Electrical` = 2, `step-val-Instrumentation` = 1. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached the elements first and stamped a zero into them. That is the precise distinction three pages in this same wave passed on (voice-journal, public-feed and engineering-design wrote no server figure at all while waiting). AND THE SKELETONS DO NOT EXCUSE IT - this page rendered **8** skeleton/shimmer elements at the same moment it wrote those zeros. Decoration and assertion are independent: a reader looking at a hero tile showing 0 is not reassured by a shimmer elsewhere on the page. This is why the oracle counts what is ASSERTED rather than what is decorated, and why a skeleton count alone was never sufficient evidence. TO FINISH (batched per A15): do not write to those hero elements until the read resolves - hold the skeleton, or write the dash sentinel. alert-hub is the reference implementation on this platform: 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact rather than an inference. findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. findings.title: axe abstains on 29 of 76 color-contrast nodes (38%) - refused rather than banked green on a minority judgement
findings.detail: THIS ROW WAS RE-EARNED, NOT RE-STAMPED. Appending one IIFE to utils.js - the correct central fix for a keyboard defect in the shared .wh-scroll-x class - changed `utils.js::toplevel`, the single R4b digest bucket covering everything outside a function body, and expired 309 banked rows across the 22 banks at once. I split that set before spending a re-walk: the 4 pages that CONTAIN .wh-scroll-x could genuinely have had their tab ring changed, and the 16 that do not could not. This page is one of the 4, so its rows were re-measured from scratch rather than argued back. AND THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED THE QUESTION IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: the helper is present (window.whEnhanceScrollRegions is a function) but on this page, in this state, 1 .wh-scroll-x element exists and it is not scrolling at any of the three widths, so 0 were made focusable - so the shared fix adds no tab stop here and could not have altered any reading. That is a fact I could only get by looking; the staling was real, its consequence here was not. REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE POINT. axe-core over the whole document (510 nodes) returns 0 violations and 25 rules passing - but the color-contrast rule judged only 47 nodes and returned INCOMPLETE on 29 of them, 38% of the total. An incomplete is axe DECLINING to judge, because it cannot resolve the element's composited background - this platform's translucent card fills over gradient backdrops are exactly that case. '0 violations' over a minority of the text is not the oracle's claim. The oracle says every text node meets 4.5:1 against its ACTUAL composited background, and 29 nodes have no verdict at all, so the honest state is OWED. Banking it green would be the false-343 shape: a real instrument, a real zero, and a denominator quietly excluding most of the subject. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED MEANWHILE, so the next walk does not start over: no node that axe COULD judge fails, and the APCA lens (row 142) measured 60 nodes on this page with 0 failing and 0 inconclusive, compositing each ancestor's background until it reaches an opaque one. APCA is the stricter perceptual standard and it resolves the alpha axe gives up on, so there is good reason to expect this page is fine - but 'expect' is not 'measured', and these are two different standards, so 142 cannot settle 141. TO CLOSE: give the surfaces axe abstains on an opaque background (the .card #162032 decision already open for Ian unblocks this class across the platform), or re-run axe against a flattened snapshot where each translucent layer is composited, and re-read the incomplete count. The target is 0 incomplete, which project-manager achieves in this same sweep - so it is reachable, not aspirational.

APCA (row 142) covers 60 nodes with 0 failing / 0 inconclusive, which is reason for confidence but is a DIFFERENT standard and cannot settle this row. findings.title: OWED, now with an EXACT uncovered set instead of a count: 4 of 29 axe abstentions are outside the lens's measured set (3 page, 1 chrome)
findings.detail: DISPOSITIONED BY EXACT SET MEMBERSHIP, NOT BY COUNT - and that change is what makes this entry worth more than the last one. live-state-runner.js stamps every node it measures with data-wh-apca="1" precisely so a caller can ask `el.hasAttribute('data-wh-apca')` per axe abstention (:857). Its own comment states why the count argument can never work: on logbook, loading 4x the content grew the lens denominator 47->219 AND the abstentions 61->249, so the gap WIDENED - the two sets overlap without either containing the other, because the lens scopes to body-minus-shared-chrome by design while axe abstains across the chrome too. PROTOCOL RUN: the lens FIRST (so the stamps exist), then axe over the whole document, then each color-contrast INCOMPLETE node resolved via its axe target selector and asked for the stamp. 0 abstentions were unresolvable on any page, so the intersection is complete rather than sampled. RESULT ON THIS PAGE: axe returned 0 color-contrast violations and abstained on 29 nodes. Of those, 25 ARE inside the lens's measured set - so they are judged, by APCA, at 60 measured / 0 failing / 0 inconclusive - and 4 are NOT (3 in page content, 1 in shared chrome). THE UNCOVERED SET: 3 x decrement buttons whose visible label is the MINUS SIGN glyph, plus the chrome dismiss 'x'. SO THE ROW STAYS OWED, but the remaining work shrank from '29 abstentions' to '4 nodes', which is the whole point of the set test. TWO CLASSES WORTH NAMING, because they are platform-wide rather than page defects: (1) SYMBOL-ONLY LABELS. The lens excludes a node whose text is pictographic and has no word character, because an emoji glyph paints in its own colours rather than the element's `color`. But a geometric or math glyph - a chevron, a minus sign - DOES paint in `color`, so excluding it drops a real contrast subject. This is the same family as the already-recorded bug where \p{Emoji_Component} matched ASCII digits and silently dropped every numeric-only KPI label. (2) FORM INPUTS. An <input>'s placeholder and value are not an own text node, so the lens does not measure them, and axe abstains because it cannot resolve their background - meaning input text contrast is judged by NOBODY on this platform. TO CLOSE: extend the lens to measure input placeholder/value colour and to treat non-emoji symbol glyphs as text, then re-run this intersection and expect 0 uncovered.

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (4 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, so the next walk starts where this one stopped.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, so the next walk starts where this one stopped. ESTABLISHED, all measured live at 390x844 as the supervisor: (1) SKILL_CONTENT holds 10 exam questions for EVERY discipline and level - Mechanical through Production Lines, levels 1-5, all 10 - so there is no missing-data blocker here. (2) openLesson('Mechanical', 1) opens #lesson-modal (display flex) and sets _activeDiscipline='Mechanical', _activeLevel=1 (a number; the level keys are strings '1'-'5', which JS property access coerces, so that is not the fault). (3) The lesson modal's own 'Take Exam ->' control is present and clicking it OPENS #exam-modal (display flex). (4) At that moment openExam's own lookup, evaluated in place, RESOLVES: SKILL_CONTENT[_activeDiscipline][_activeLevel] returns {title, module, exam} with exam.length === 10. (5) And yet _examQuestions.length === 0, #exam-options-wrap is empty, and #exam-next-btn stays disabled - so the exam cannot be submitted and none of these four oracles has an action to grade. NOT YET ISOLATED: why the assignment _examQuestions = content.exam (skillmatrix.html:1295) does not take effect even though the right-hand side demonstrably holds 10 items at that instant. Candidates to check next, in order: whether the 'Take Exam ->' listener actually reaches openExam() or whether something else opens the modal; whether a draft-restore path or closeExam() resets _examQuestions after the assignment; and whether renderExamQuestion() throws before painting. ONE FALSE LEAD RULED OUT AND RECORDED so it is not chased again: my first walk passed openLesson the key 'mechanical' (lowercase). That is not a SKILL_CONTENT key - they are title-case - so openExam's 'if (!content) return;' guard correctly declined, and the empty exam I first saw was MY bad key, not a page defect. Also noted for the next walk: the caller above openLesson enforces a retake COOLDOWN ('Retake available in Xh Ym'), so a recent attempt on the same discipline/level will block a fresh one.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

observed.not_green_because: a journey that cannot be constructed is unbuilt, not passing
observed.to_settle: add the missing composer to dialog_targets.mjs, or declared-na under R10 with the CO family as replacement

evidence.asserts: Abandoning an exam midway leaves NOTHING half-applied where it would matter: no grading call is made, no attempt row is created, and no badge is awarded - a walked-away exam is simply an exam not taken, which on a page whose write is a credential is the only safe outcome. The work is not thrown away either: answers are held in a per-worker, per-discipline, per-level draft (wh_exam_draft_Leandro Marquez_Mechanical_3) that survives leaving the exam entirely, and returning restores the answered options rather than presenting a blank paper. RECORDED, because it is real and I would rather state it than smooth it: the draft persists ONE BEHIND. Three questions were answered before abandoning and the draft held two, so the most recent answer is lost and the person returns to that question blank. That is a small data-loss nuance rather than the half-applied state this row is about - nothing was written anywhere - but it is a genuine imperfection in the resume path.
evidence.checked: The grading RPC was intercepted so no credential could land, and the tables were counted either side (attempts 158, badges 148, both unchanged). Abandonment was real - leaving the exam surface entirely and re-entering through openDiscipline -> openLesson -> openExam - rather than merely re-rendering the modal, and the draft was read out of storage and PARSED to count answers rather than being accepted as 'has content', which is what exposed the one-behind lag.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

findings.title: LEFT OWED AS A SPLIT RESULT, because this view has two kinds of entry and only one of them is correctable - and banking green on the easy one would be measuring the wrong thing.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED AS A SPLIT RESULT, because this view has two kinds of entry and only one of them is correctable - and banking green on the easy one would be measuring the wrong thing. skill_profiles writes were HELD (counted, 600ms, fulfilled locally; nothing written to the shared test DB). WHAT WORKS, and works well: the TARGETS are adjusted in place with per-discipline minus/plus steppers (no selects - the row is a stepper pair), and 'Save Targets' disables itself to 'Saving...' on press, issues exactly ONE upsert, restores its label, and confirms with '✓ Targets saved -> your skill gaps and available quizzes update now.' - which names the effect a person can look for rather than just acknowledging the click. Set a target wrong, move the stepper, save again: corrected without starting over. The page's own copy promises exactly this ('You can adjust targets anytime') and the promise holds. WHAT CANNOT BE CORRECTED AT ALL: the PRIMARY DISCIPLINE. It is chosen once in #onboarding-section, which renders only when `!_profile`, and after that there is no affordance anywhere to change it - confirmed two independent ways: a live survey of every visible button found nothing matching discipline/primary/change/switch (the full visible set is the steppers, 'Save Targets', 'Show details', 'Growth', 'Back'), and a source grep for a change/switch-discipline control finds none. The held upsert payload shows primary_skill ('Steam Systems') is SENT on every target save via onConflict worker_name, so the value round-trips continuously while never being editable. WHY THIS IS THE REAL FINDING: the primary discipline frames the whole matrix - it drives the discipline colour, the level-5 target default, and which quizzes are surfaced - and it is picked on a worker's very first visit from a three-option picker, before they have seen what it does. Get it wrong and the matrix is permanently framed around the wrong trade, with no in-product recovery; the onboarding copy promises adjustable TARGETS and says nothing about the primary being a one-time choice. RELATED AND ALREADY FIXED, recorded so it is not re-hunted: a failed profile read used to render that same first-run picker to a worker who HAS a profile, where picking would overwrite the profile the page merely could not read. That is closed - `_smReadFailed` now gates it, the failure renders into its own sibling node (#sm-read-failed) rather than replacing #onboarding-section's contents, and the message reads 'Your levels are unknown right now, not zero. Do not re-pick your discipline; your profile is saved.' WHAT A FIX NEEDS, with the design questions named rather than guessed: a change-primary control is mechanically easy (the upsert already carries primary_skill on onConflict worker_name), but it is not a mechanical change - it must decide whether switching the primary RESETS the target defaults (primary L5 / others L2) or preserves the worker's customised targets, and what happens to badges already earned under the old framing. Those are product semantics, so they are recorded here rather than invented.

evidence.asserts: a level entered wrongly can be corrected in place - the same control accepts the correction immediately, with no reload, no reset and no re-entry of anything else
evidence.checked: Driven live on the matrix, with every write intercepted so nothing persisted to the shared database. THE ROUND TRIP: the Mechanical level read 3; pressing + moved it to 4 (the wrong entry); pressing - moved it back to 3 (the correction). Both steps took effect on the SAME control, the control remained present and usable throughout, and no reload, reset or start-over flow was required at any point - which is precisely what this oracle asks. MY FIRST ATTEMPT REPORTED A FAILURE AND IT WAS MINE, NOT THE PAGE'S: clicking + twice then - twice in quick succession took 3 to 4 to 2, so the round trip did not return to start and my equality assertion failed. The cause was pacing - one + click landed while a write was still in flight and did not register, while both - clicks did. Re-run with each step allowed to settle, the round trip is exact. The lesson is that a stepper bound to a persisted value needs its changes serialised before the next input, or the probe measures its own haste; the page was correcting faithfully the whole time. Non-vacuity: the wrong entry demonstrably CHANGED the value (3 -> 4) before the correction restored it, so this is a real edit-and-undo rather than two no-ops. Read-only in effect: mutating requests were intercepted and answered locally, so the worker's real skill level was never altered.
evidence.value_checked: #step-val-Mechanical: start=3, after + =4 (wrong entry registered), after - =3 (corrected); same control used for both, still present afterwards; no reload or reset flow; writes intercepted, none persisted

evidence.asserts: after acting, the person is told whether it landed
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_did_it_land.mjs: 26 controls driven, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 ungraded - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE, every mutating request intercepted and answered in-page. ★THE QUESTION IS THE ONE A PERSON ASKS WITH THEIR THUMB STILL ON THE SCREEN: did that land? A surface that takes a press and says nothing leaves them to guess, and the guess is almost always 'do it again' - which is how a duplicate gets created. So the oracle is not 'did the write succeed' but 'was the person TOLD', and the two come apart exactly when the network is slow. ★AND IT IS ANSWERED BY ACTING, WHICH IS WHY THE INTERCEPTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT. Every other check in this bank can be answered by looking; this one presses real controls on a live product. The requests are counted and answered inside the page so the probe cannot perform the thing it means to observe - a discipline this platform bought the hard way, when an earlier sweep hunting for a refusal ACTIVATED A SUCCESS because its filter excluded delete/pay but not save/generate. FOR THIS PAGE: 1 control(s) pressed. Each one told the person the outcome rather than leaving them to infer it. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.
