findings.title: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, so the next walk starts where this one stopped.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED with a full diagnosis rather than graded, so the next walk starts where this one stopped. ESTABLISHED, all measured live at 390x844 as the supervisor: (1) SKILL_CONTENT holds 10 exam questions for EVERY discipline and level - Mechanical through Production Lines, levels 1-5, all 10 - so there is no missing-data blocker here. (2) openLesson('Mechanical', 1) opens #lesson-modal (display flex) and sets _activeDiscipline='Mechanical', _activeLevel=1 (a number; the level keys are strings '1'-'5', which JS property access coerces, so that is not the fault). (3) The lesson modal's own 'Take Exam ->' control is present and clicking it OPENS #exam-modal (display flex). (4) At that moment openExam's own lookup, evaluated in place, RESOLVES: SKILL_CONTENT[_activeDiscipline][_activeLevel] returns {title, module, exam} with exam.length === 10. (5) And yet _examQuestions.length === 0, #exam-options-wrap is empty, and #exam-next-btn stays disabled - so the exam cannot be submitted and none of these four oracles has an action to grade. NOT YET ISOLATED: why the assignment _examQuestions = content.exam (skillmatrix.html:1295) does not take effect even though the right-hand side demonstrably holds 10 items at that instant. Candidates to check next, in order: whether the 'Take Exam ->' listener actually reaches openExam() or whether something else opens the modal; whether a draft-restore path or closeExam() resets _examQuestions after the assignment; and whether renderExamQuestion() throws before painting. ONE FALSE LEAD RULED OUT AND RECORDED so it is not chased again: my first walk passed openLesson the key 'mechanical' (lowercase). That is not a SKILL_CONTENT key - they are title-case - so openExam's 'if (!content) return;' guard correctly declined, and the empty exam I first saw was MY bad key, not a page defect. Also noted for the next walk: the caller above openLesson enforces a retake COOLDOWN ('Retake available in Xh Ym'), so a recent attempt on the same discipline/level will block a fresh one.

observed.ruled_out: lowercase discipline key was my error, not a defect

evidence.asserts: the exam cannot be submitted incomplete, and completing the missing answer is all it takes
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK. This view PREVENTS rather than refuses, at TWO gates. First, the exam cannot even be STARTED until the lesson is read: #lesson-exam-btn ships disabled with #lesson-scroll-hint shown, and checkScroll enables it only near the bottom of #lesson-body-scroll - measured disabled on open and enabled after scrolling. Second, inside the exam #exam-next-btn is disabled until the current question is answered, measured at question 1 of 10 with nothing selected. So there is no incomplete submission to recover from. Nothing typed can be lost because nothing is typed - answers are single-choice selections, each persisted to a per-discipline localStorage draft (wh_exam_draft_<worker>_<disc>_<level>) as it is made, so an interruption mid-exam does not cost the answers already given. AN EXAM COULD BE GRADED OVER AND OVER, AND THAT IS FIXED THIS WALK. Measured with RPCs intercepted so nothing landed: after all ten answers, #exam-next-btn KEPT the label 'Next ->', stayed ENABLED, and every further press called submitExam() again - five presses produced FIVE rpc/grade_skill_exam calls. _examSubmitted was already being set to true, and nothing ever read it. This platform's own invariant is 'one submission -> one attempt and at most one badge; a double-submit creates neither a second attempt nor a second badge', and a badge here is a claim about someone's qualifications that the hive board and achievements both read. Fixed on both halves: the click handler refuses re-entry on _examSubmitted or a disabled button, shows 'Grading...' with aria-busy, and restores submittability if the grade throws (one network blip must not end an attempt); and the button RELABELS to 'Submit exam' on the last question, because the press that commits a credential had looked identical to the nine that merely moved forward. Re-measured: ONE grade call. REACHED THROUGH THE REAL GATE, and that gate is the correction carried by this row. openLesson('Mechanical', 1) opens the lesson with #lesson-exam-btn DISABLED and #lesson-scroll-hint visible; checkScroll enables the button only once #lesson-body-scroll is scrolled near its bottom. The walk now scrolls to the end, ASSERTS the button was disabled before that (were it already enabled, the read-before-tested gate would not be holding and this row would say so), clicks Take Exam, answers all ten using the page's OWN answer key so the PASS branch - the one that awards the credential - is what gets graded, and submits. A CLAIM I MADE EARLIER IS WITHDRAWN HERE: I recorded that clicking the visible Take Exam control left _examQuestions at 0 while openExam() worked directly, and flagged it as a candidate defect in the lesson handler. It is NOT a defect. The button is disabled until the lesson is read - deliberately, with a visible hint - so my click never dispatched, and my walk's openExam() fallback was BYPASSING a working gate rather than exposing a broken one. Two of my own measuring errors hid this: I tested modal visibility with display !== 'none', but .modal-overlay rests at display:flex on this page and is hidden by opacity and pointer-events, so 'the exam modal opened' was vacuously true every time; and I never checked the button's disabled state.
